summary: Preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executes obfuscated payload under Bun
details: @servicetitan/micro-frontend@0.0.6 declares `scripts.preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (oven-sh/bun v1.3.13) from GitHub releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})` on `npm install`. The bundled `math_init.js` is a ~727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) with hex-mangled identifiers, a large numeric constant array, and a string-array rotator function (`WV8StW` shifting `n7gIxM`) — classic string-array obfuscation. The tiny React library under `dist/` never references `math_init.js`; the file is reachable only through the preinstall Bun exec. A React micro-frontend library has no legitimate need to fetch a JavaScript runtime and use it to execute an unrelated 727KB obfuscated bundle at install time; using Bun rather than Node evades Node-based install-time inspection. The package is published under the `@servicetitan` scope with a repository URL pointing at `github.com/servicetitan/playground.git`, consistent with unauthorized publication under a trusted vendor namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
